title: Astra v7 synthesis was fed an empty claim-honesty section (builder picked the gemini validation file)
what_went_wrong: build_astra_task_r7.py load_prior() took sorted(glob('astra_v7_step1_*_output.md'))[-1]. The glob also matches astra_v7_step1_validation_gemini_4880116_output.md, which sorts after the astra file and has an empty CLAIM-HONESTY section.

The merged v7 task (Kaggle version 9) therefore embedded PRIOR = {'claim-honesty': ''}; the synthesis (gpt-6-astra run 4894730) stated 'The claim-honesty section is empty' and scored claim-honesty 6/10 from the other sections' contradictions.
The dry run with a fake model checked section splitting and the synthesis digest keys, but not that the embedded prior text was non-empty.
root_cause: A selection-by-glob over a folder holding two kinds of outputs with a shared prefix; no assertion that an embedded prior section is non-empty.
detection: The orchestrator read the v7 verdict text before reporting it (2026-10-18 local) and traced the 'section is empty' remark to the embedded PRIOR.
impact: None on the score arithmetic: step 1's real claim-honesty score is also 6/10 (run 4880158), so v7 = round(35 x 10/6) = 58/100 either way. The synthesis did not read step 1's findings. Owner chose to accept 58 with this caveat rather than spend ~$0.5 of the $8 monthly budget on a synthesis re-run.

correction.code: load_prior() excludes '_validation_' files; rebuilt task embeds claim-honesty (11,747 chars).
correction.record: As-run task reconstructed as tools/kaggle/task_r7_merged_asrun_v9.py (258,648 bytes, the size Kaggle accepted); caveat recorded in evidence/astra_v7_merged_4894730_NOTE.md.
correction.verification: Rebuilt merged task: PRIOR claim-honesty length 11,747, starts with step 1's '6/10' verdict line.

rule: When a builder embeds earlier outputs, assert each embedded section is non-empty and name the source file in the build log; never select evidence by an unqualified glob in a folder of mixed output kinds.
